title: Strict quotient-system finite exceptional mapping adjunction
statement:
theorem integralDualizing_system_finite_adjunction
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (G : CoefPairingSystem l E (finiteDualizingCompactification D X) S)
    (Q : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
    (eQ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).obj (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≅
        integralDualizingFiniteTerm l E D X n)
    (hQ : ∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m),
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E X h).app (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≫
          (normalizedDVRRes l E X h).map (eQ n).hom =
        (eQ m).hom ≫
          (Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (normalizedDVRRes l E X h)).homEquiv _ _
            (integralDualizingFiniteComparison l E D X hl h)) :
    Nonempty ((sfIntegralConstructible l E X).ι.op ⋙ coefPairingHom l E X S Q ≅
      integralDualizingSupportSystemHom D l E X S G)

proof.text: Obtain a normalized trace on Q; it involves no test input. Form the explicit exceptional transpose natural transformation.

For each constructible input separately, every exact scalar-tower evaluation of that already constructed map is invertible by the finite exceptional mapping adjunction. Joint conservativity makes its component invertible. Componentwise invertibility makes the natural transformation a natural isomorphism.
